rationale: This is a mechanical splice of three archive signals — QualityIndexProfit with the profitability leg swapped for the already-tested R&D-restored version — with no new economic content beyond what IntangibleProfitConservatism and IntangibleProfitRollover jointly established, so it is effectively a rediscovery/cosmetic recombination rather than a new hypothesis.

Beyond being a four-component kitchen-sink of already-tested legs (dp intensity, dlc/lt from ShortDebtShareProfit, act/lct from IntangibleProfitWithSlack), the nested SUMRANK silently weights conservatism at 50% and each funding component at 25%, which contradicts the stated "three separable aspects" framing and makes any result uninterpretable as a test of dimensionality.

The floor-vs-level question is a legitimate persistence test, but it is asked here by stacking three previously validated components at once (TS_MIN from ProfitFloorConservatism, R&D restoration, and the two-part quality index), so a change in alpha cannot be attributed to the floor construction — the clean version would vary only TS_MIN against an existing archive baseline.

This is the only proposal that fixes a real measurement asymmetry rather than reshuffling legs — capitalizing the R&D stock in the denominator directly tests whether the intangible premium is productivity or a mechanical numerator inflation — though the construction is internally half-consistent (full current-year spend is added back with no amortization charge against the capitalized stock) and the R&D-capitalization idea itself is well-trodden in the literature.

Filling the {stability}×{conservatism} cell of the 2×2 is a defensible isolated design test given FragileEarningsRollover worked, but note it discards the profitability level entirely, so a positive result may simply reload the well-known low-earnings-volatility quality anomaly interacted with an asset-age/capital-intensity proxy, and the hypothesis text sloppily calls high dp intensity "aggressive depreciation" where the rest of the archive calls it conservative.

This is explicitly the same economic content as proposal 1 with only the aggregation operator changed — a textbook cosmetic variant, and one whose rank-product form is already the dominant construction throughout the archive, so it adds no information the existing pairwise multiplicative signals have not already provided.
